grounding.derivation: pending-read-intent describes this particular internal queue as holding reads that cannot be answered before a new leader commits in its term, and says they will be handled as fast as the first log is committed in that term. Interpret this as a local transition responsibility: after the first-current-term commitment transition completes, a request already held solely on that condition must be released from this waiting queue for ordinary read processing. The expectation is attributed to that specific implementation statement, not inferred solely from differing call sites. Public ReadIndex explicitly allows requests to be lost and requires retry; this is not a claim of unconditional read completion, linearizability violation or an elapsed-time deadline.
grounding.applicability: Synchronous public Node, ReadOnlySafe, surviving leader and unique request context, real pending request before first-current-term commit. Membership activation or an append reply can establish that commit condition. Early Advance is permitted by the Node and doc.go interface statements, with Ready application order retained.
alternatives: Public read completion can require retries; a missing ReadState alone would not violate this local queue-release proposition.
The append-reply path explicitly releases this queue; membership activation must be examined separately.
